chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Qalla' said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man whose brother died and left a chest of pledges (rhn); some of it had the owner's name on it and its pledge value was known, while for some no one knew who they belonged to or what their pledge value was. What do you think regarding that which has no known owner? He said, 'It is [distributed] like its entirety.'

key_terms.رُهُوناً: pledges or items held as security/guarantee

ai.seo_question: How to distribute pledged items from a deceased's estate when the owners are unknown?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) addresses the fiqh of *rhn* (pledges) where the owners of some items are unknown. He rules that the value of these unidentified pledges should be treated 'as their whole' (kamaalihi), meaning they are assessed and distributed in proportion to the known pledges, ensuring equitable treatment for the unknown owners. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of preserving the rights of absent parties in inheritance and debt settlements through proportional valuation.
